$comment: Accepted merge-gate policy for `main`. This file is the written intent;
`scripts/check-workflow-policy.mjs` is what makes it true. Offline it
reconciles this policy against the workflow files that actually produce the
contexts; with `--live` it also reads back the repository settings and the
`main` ruleset. Both directions fail: a context here that no workflow emits,
and a pull-request job that no entry claims.
`class` records the authority of a check, which is not the same question as
required     a merge gate; must be emitted on every ordinary pull request
staged       intended to become required, held back until observed stable
advisory     reports, never blocks (path-filtered or scheduled coverage)
automation   repository automation, not a statement about the change

contexts.proves: The extension crate formats, passes clippy with warnings denied, passes `cargo test --locked`, and builds for `wasm32-wasip2` — the target the extension registry ships. It does not prove anything about Spring Tools behaviour.
Coordinator and repository-check tests pass, and the derivable records — contributors list, third-party notices, Spring Tools pin inventory — match the tree they describe.
The dependency diff this pull request introduces carries no known advisory at moderate or above. Scoped to the diff only; the standing graph is Dependabot's.

actionlint, zizmor and this policy check all pass, so no workflow carries a mutable action ref, a missing timeout, an unsafe `pull_request_target` checkout, or a context that has drifted from this file.
contexts.promotion_evidence: Observed passing on ordinary pull requests and merged `main`; authoritative live audit run 34118039906 on exact `main` d07834ddf9a10bee23e6868ba610f18bf21d77c3 confirmed repository settings and the pre-promotion live ruleset matched this policy before the required-context migration.

contexts.proves: Each Linux, macOS, and Windows x86_64/arm64 leg runs on its native GitHub-hosted architecture with JDK 25, Node 24, and Rust 1.98.0. Linux/macOS drive every existing coordinator contract directly; Windows drives every platform-neutral contract and proof-equivalent native path/wall-clock replacements for seven legacy fixture-bound forms. Every leg also runs the Java bridge self-test, native Rust tests, native path/wrapper checks, and checksum-verifies then launches the canonical pinned Spring Tools runtime for real headless LSP initialize/open/completion/hover/shutdown traffic. It is still not integrated Zed + official Java/JDT runtime evidence.

The canonical pinned Spring Tools runtime checksum-verifies, starts with the production Spring JVM launch vector, serves real headless LSP traffic, and terminates under the declared JDK 21 floor on Linux x86_64. Host portability remains owned by the six-tuple `platform` matrix; this context does not prove integrated Zed + official Java/JDT behaviour.

All six native `platform` matrix legs and the independent JDK 21 `spring-runtime-floor` job completed successfully for the same workflow revision. This is the stable aggregate context intended for later ruleset promotion after it has demonstrated ordinary-PR and merged-main stability.

CodeQL findings for one language reach the Security tab. Deliberately never required: `codeql.yml` ignores documentation-only changes, so the context legitimately disappears on the bulk of this repository's traffic, and a required check that vanishes is a gate in name only.

Nothing about the change. Applies additive routing labels on `pull_request` for same-repository branches only; fork pull requests are intentionally skipped because their read-only token cannot write labels. It is automation metadata, never a merge gate.
